segments.text: We will connect source, build and test,
approval, and deploy. The example
verifies artifact identity, publishes
Pytest results, blocks for unsafe cases,
and never touches a real cloud account.
The pipeline orders stages and passes
artifacts. A build project gets source,
follows buildspec.yml,
installs tools, builds output, runs
tests, and returns status and files.
Create the output, record revision and
digest, verify the file, run Pytest with
JUnit XML, read the report, and state
the exact conditions that allow
deployment. Source produces source
output. Build and test consumes it and
produces tested output. Approval pauses
the flow. Deploy may consume only the
tested output after approval. Queued
mode processes V2 pipeline executions
one by one. Parallel mode runs
independently and does not support stage
rollback. Choose mode from target
behavior, not speed alone. Buildspec
version 0.2 defines install and build
phases, reports, artifacts, and cache
paths. Keep the file with source so
changes can be reviewed. The runtime is
currently available on supported
standard Linux images. The project image
and buildspec runtime must agree.
Recheck both before real run. Install
phase uses Python -m pip, store secrets
outside the buildspec and pipeline
fields. Give a build role only the
resources this job needs.
The manifest records the artifact path,
source revision, and SHA-256
digest. The next command hashes the file
and stops if it changed. Exit zero means
pass, one means a failed test, and five
means no tests were collected. The
pipeline must stop on one or five
instead of continuing toward deployment.
The report section names the report
group, file, base directory, and JUnit
format. The report helps investigation.
The command exit code still decides
whether the build action passed.
The artifact section lists exact files
and keeps their directory paths.
Downstream actions receive tested
output. Check encryption, permissions,
identity, and retention.
Approval is not a test. The reviewer
checks the revision, report, artifact
digest, target change window, and
recovery plan. Rejection or no response
stops the execution. The local gate
requires command exit zero, at least one
test, zero failures, valid artifact
identity, and approved review. One
missing fact blocks deployment.
Only the all good case can pass the
gate. A failed test, empty test run,
rejected approval, or changed artifact
produces a clear blocking reason.
Stage rollback can use a previous
successful execution when the pipeline
structure supports it. Parallel mode
cannot use stage rollback. Test recovery
on a safe target first.
Do not place secret values in pipeline
fields or logs. Use least access,
protected secret storage, encrypted
artifact storage, separate roles, and an
audit trail for approvals and changes.
Private test account must prove action
roles, source revision, image, commands,
report group, artifact bucket, approval
rights, execution mode, deployment
target, rollback, and reback.
Confirm execution ID, revision, artifact
names, build ID, test count, failure
details, digest, approval identity,
target version, health checks, logs,
cost, cleanup, and recovery result. Run
the local demo now. When an authorized
test account is ready, validate one
non-production execution. Next, we test
the container on every change with
Google Cloud Build.
